{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''John Howard Smith''' is an American [[mathematician]] and retired professor of mathematics at [[Boston College]].<ref name="bu">[http://www.bc.edu/schools/cas/math/newsinfo/faculty.html Math faculty listing], Boston College, retrieved 2011-03-28.</ref> He received his Ph.D. from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1963, under the supervision of [[Kenkichi Iwasawa]].<ref name="bu"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=John Howard Smith|id=7805}}.</ref>
In [[voting theory]], he is known for the [[Smith set]], the smallest nonempty set of candidates such that, in every pairwise matchup (two-candidate election/runoff) between a member and a non-member, the member is the winner by majority rule, and for the [[Smith criterion]], a property of certain election systems in which the winner is guaranteed to belong to the Smith set.<ref>{{citation | last=Smith | first= J.H. | title=Aggregation of Preferences with Variable Electorates | journal=Econometrica | year=1973 | volume=41 | pages=1027–1041 | doi=10.2307/1914033 | jstor=1914033 | issue=6}}.</ref> He has also made contributions to [[spectral graph theory]]<ref>{{citation
 | last = Smith | first = John H.
 | contribution = Some properties of the spectrum of a graph
 | mr = 0266799
 | location = New York
 | pages = 403–406
 | publisher = Gordon and Breach
 | title = Combinatorial Structures and their Applications (Proc. Calgary Internat. Conf., Calgary, Alta., 1969)
 | year = 1970}}.</ref> and [[additive number theory]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Fein | first1 = Burton
 | last2 = Gordon | first2 = Basil | author2-link = Basil Gordon
 | last3 = Smith | first3 = John H.
 | doi = 10.1016/0022-314X(71)90005-9
 | mr = 0319940
 | journal = Journal of Number Theory
 | pages = 310–315
 | title = On the representation of &minus;1 as a sum of two squares in an algebraic number field
 | volume = 3
 | year = 1971| issue = 3
 | doi-access = 
 }}.</ref>
